title: U.S. House · Idaho's 2nd District
area: Eastern Idaho, including Idaho Falls, Pocatello, Twin Falls, and Boise's eastern portion.

context.text: Incumbent Michael K. Simpson defeated Brian Keene and Perry Shumway in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 63.3% of the vote. Elinor Gilbreath defeated Julie Wiley (who unofficially withdrew) in the Democratic primary with 72.5% of the vote. Will Johanson advanced from the Libertarian primary; Idaho Law (Constitution Party) is listed as withdrawn or disqualified and does not appear in the general election.
The Cook Political Report rates this district R+13 by partisan voting index.

summary.text: Michael K. Simpson is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Idaho's 2nd District. He was born in Cassia County, Idaho, worked as a dentist, served in the Idaho House, and has served on the House Appropriations Committee throughout his time in Congress.

background.text: Graduated from Blackfoot High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Utah State University and a degree in dental medicine from Washington University.
Worked as a dentist and served in the Idaho House of Representatives before being elected to Congress.

priorities.text: Says he continuously opposed proposals to grant amnesty to illegal aliens and has worked to increase funding to combat illegal immigration and expedite the construction of a border fence.

Says he is troubled by the growing federal debt and supports drastically reducing discretionary spending, reforming entitlement programs, and passing a balanced-budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
Says the country should pursue a comprehensive energy strategy that includes nuclear power, energy efficiency, and renewable energy alongside continued development of oil and natural gas.

positions.summary: Says he has supported legislation allowing law enforcement to keep weapons, narcotics, and smugglers out of the country and to expedite the removal of criminal aliens, and is working on legislation to increase funding to combat illegal immigration.
positions.quote: I have supported legislation which allows law enforcement to do what is necessary to keep harmful weapons, narcotics, and smugglers out of our country and expedites the removal of criminal aliens.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025-2026 Congress, chairing the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies subcommittee, and also sitting on the Labor-HHS-Education and Energy-Water Development subcommittees.
Chaired the Interior and Environment appropriations subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress and served as ranking member of the Energy and Water Development subcommittee in 2021-2022.

candidates.name: Elinor Gilbreath

summary.text: Elinor (Ellie) Gilbreath is the Democratic nominee for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. She has more than 20 years of experience in conflict resolution and mediation.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, Los Angeles, and a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center.
Has worked as a mediator with more than 20 years of experience in conflict resolution.

priorities.text: Says her priorities are restoring accountability and balance in government, protecting Idaho's public lands, water, and energy, and lowering the cost of living for Idaho families, including access to affordable healthcare.
Says she will focus on protecting fundamental freedoms and ensuring government works for everyone rather than special interests.
priorities.quote: From freedom of speech to the Second Amendment, I believe upholding the rule of law and that laws must be applied evenly and lawfully—without favoritism, political weaponization, or selective enforcement.

positions.summary: Her campaign policies page calls for fully funding Medicare and Medicaid and restoring ACA tax credits.
Her campaign policies page calls for closing tax loopholes that favor corporations and the ultra-wealthy and for collecting unpaid taxes owed by billionaires.
positions.quote: Close the loopholes that favor corporations and the ultra-wealthy.

positions.summary: In the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire, says documentary proof of citizenship requirements in the SAVE Act create barriers for eligible citizens.
positions.quote: Requiring documentary proof of citizenship creates barriers for Americans who are unquestionably eligible: veterans, elderly citizens, rural Idahoans, and married women who’ve legally changed their names.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from her campaign policies page and the Idaho Capital Sun 2026 voter guide questionnaire. She did not respond to the CBS2/FOX9 survey. Her answers on abortion and guns appear only in a radio interview summary (not her verbatim words), so none were recorded.

statements.quote: Adjust tariffs, return Constitutional controls to Congress, lowering the cost of groceries, farm supplies, and construction.
Lower the cost of housing by expanding the ROAD to Housing Act, cutting more red tape, funding rural housing, and outright banning corporate purchase of single-family homes.
Lower rental rates by preventing algorithm-based price-fixing by property management companies, which has cost Idahoans hundreds of millions of dollars.
America is a closed border nation. We need a strong secure border.
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide questionnaire

candidates.name: Will Johanson

summary.text: Will Johanson is the Libertarian Party nominee for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District, having advanced from the Libertarian primary on May 19, 2026.

priorities.text: In the CBS2/FOX9 survey, names affordability as the biggest issue and says his plan is to vote no on increased warfare spending, subsidies, and taxes on the working class.
priorities.quote: “No” to increased spending on warfare we cannot afford; “no” to subsidies for corporations, foreign governments, and the permanent able-bodied welfare class; and “no” to increased taxes on the working class.

priorities.text: Says Congress should balance the budget, address healthcare costs, and address immigration.
priorities.quote: Congress tackle three issues head on: balancing the budget, healthcare, and immigration.

priorities.text: Says he would introduce legislation to abolish the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
priorities.quote: I pledge to introduce legislation to abolish the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and replace it or move its duties to another agency in the Department of Energy that has not proven its hostility to nuclear power.

candidates.researchNotes: Source is the CBS2/FOX9 Idaho candidate survey (Aug. 2026), where answers are the candidate's own words. He did not respond to the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire; no campaign website or Ballotpedia survey was loaded. His statements do not squarely take a side on the guide's issue statements, so no stances were recorded.

statements.quote: the runaway immigration—both legal and illegal—depresses wages, drives up the cost of housing, and makes our communities less safe.
statements.context: In the CBS2/FOX9 candidate survey, Aug. 2026

statements.quote: healthcare costs have gone completely out of control, and the root cause is our tangled web of regulation that benefits the largest corporations and stifles free-market competition.
statements.context: In the CBS2/FOX9 candidate survey, Aug. 2026

candidates.name: Emre Houser

summary.text: Emre Houser is an Independent candidate running in the general election for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District.

priorities.text: Platform pledges to oppose the sale of public lands.
priorities.quote: I will not allow our beloved public lands be sold to the highest bidder for them to just put up fences and road blocks to deny access.

priorities.text: Platform calls for term limits and a ban on individual stock trading by members of Congress.
priorities.quote: I believe that members of Congress should not be allowed to invest in individual stocks and bonds while serving in Congress.

priorities.text: Platform calls for breaking up monopolies and mega corporations.
priorities.quote: We need LESS mega-corporations influence and MORE competition which benefit farmers and consumers.

positions.summary: His campaign platform calls for ending tax loopholes and the "buy, borrow, die" system, and for removing the Social Security wage cap.
positions.quote: End the system of buy, borrow, die, which allows the ultra wealthy to avoid paying taxes.

positions.summary: His campaign platform says current tariffs raise household costs but that responsible tariffs are useful in limited circumstances.
positions.quote: I believe responsible tariffs are a useful tool in limited circumstances. However, we need to get back to responsible tariffs and reform our relationships with other countries who not only rely on us, but with whom we rely on for goods.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from the Platform page of his campaign site (houserforidaho.com). He did not respond to the CBS2/FOX9 survey or the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire. The site's tax and tariff text is quoted as written.

statements.quote: ICE raids keep legal workers home. Not having our workers safely making it to their jobs hurts every industry and will be felt in every corner of our state.
statements.context: On the Agricultural Support section of his campaign platform page

statements.quote: If the drug prices that the Veterans Administration pays for drugs were applied to Medicare and Medicaid, the estimated annual savings for the Government and copays would range from $20-$40 billion per year.
statements.context: On the Medical Spending Savings section of his campaign platform page

candidates.name: Tripp Hutchinson

summary.text: Tripp Hutchinson is an Independent candidate running in the general election for Idaho's 2nd Congressional District. The Idaho Mountain Express reported (Apr. 6, 2026) that in 5th District Court he was sentenced on March 31, 2026 on one misdemeanor count of petit theft under a plea deal accepted in February, to 12 months of probation and 40 hours of community service, with restitution of $3,513.19 to Friedman Memorial Airport; the judge granted withheld judgment until March 31, 2027, so the guilty plea is not formally entered and the case could be dismissed if he follows probation terms. The report says he cited "moral civil disobedience" as his reason.

priorities.text: In the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire, lists protecting public lands, ending mass surveillance, and breaking up big-agriculture monopolies as his top priorities.
priorities.quote: Protect Public Lands, End Mass Surveillance, Break Up Big-Agriculture Monopolies.

priorities.text: Says Congress must act on affordability, including housing, wages, unions and parental leave.
priorities.quote: Every Idaho family should be able to live a normal, fulfilled and decent life on one household income.

positions.summary: In the CBS2/FOX9 survey, says Congress must raise the minimum wage.
positions.quote: Congress must raise the minimum wage, bolster unions, expand parental leave, create more housing and break up the monopolies that have destroyed competition and corroded the American dream.

positions.summary: In the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire, says he is working toward a public single-payer system.
positions.quote: Take on Big Pharma Monopolies and Insurance Monopolies while also working towards a public single-payer system.

positions.summary: Asked in the Idaho Capital Sun questionnaire whether he supports the SAVE Act, which requires proof of citizenship to register, says he does not.
positions.quote: I do not. The legislation is blatant voter suppression.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his own written answers in the CBS2/FOX9 survey (Aug. 2026) and the Idaho Capital Sun 2026 voter guide. No campaign website was loaded. His March 2026 misdemeanor sentencing is described in his summary (Idaho Mountain Express).

statements.quote: Congress needs to legislate a much more efficient and robust pathway to citizenship for law abiding immigrants that are already in our country.
statements.context: In the Idaho Capital Sun voter guide questionnaire
